note: What and Why are verbatim from Research. How and Caveats are verbatim where they carry no figures; where they do, the page's own method text from the data files is shown instead.

tiles.independence: Independence is whether a client is its own codebase or is derived from Bitcoin Core. A fork can change policy and still share the same code, so a bug can travel with that lineage.
tiles.assurance: Assurance is how far a client has gone in showing it follows Bitcoin's rules. The six layers are a written spec, shared test vectors, property tests, fuzzing, formal proofs, and comparison with Core.
tiles.accountability: Accountability is who can change a client's code and how. Projects are read as a single maintainer, a maintainer group, a foundation signing key, written rules published by Bitcoin Commons, or not classified.

how_to_read: The page is organized on three axes: independence (own codebase or Core-derived), assurance (the six-layer verification stack), and accountability (who can change the code and how). Code-health figures sit under those axes; they are sizes and counts, not grades.

Assurance radials score yes = 2, partial = 1, and not found = 0. That rule is printed on the page. A not-measured, partial, or n/a cell is a gap or hatch, never a zero. A missing spoke is not a weak score.
"Not found" means no public source turned up. It does not mean the project lacks the thing.
Every numeric cell is dated (this reading: 2026-11-12) and pinned to a commit. Sources open under the row. Author and release counts use the 12 months from 2025-11-12 to 2026-11-12.
Rules share uses three different cuts. Those percentages are not comparable across cuts. Several rules-share cells are not measured, including BLVM's.
Size and composition tables cover nine trees. Floresta, rbitcoin, and btcd appear in the other tables but have no size row.
Some checkouts are shallow. Process figures for Bitcoin Core come from cited research reports and are not scored this week for the H2–H6 rows.
The implementation is called BLVM. "Bitcoin Commons" names the written governance rules.
No chart or caption on this page claims a full-chain differential result.

entries.name: Lineage (Core-derived vs separate codebase)
entries.what: Whether the tree is Bitcoin Core, is stated as built from Core or from Bitcoin Knots, or is a separate codebase.
entries.why: Clients that share a lineage can share a bug. Moving to a Core-derived client can change policy without changing the code underneath.
entries.how: Derived from `data/implementations.json` `class` and `governance.history`, as quoted by `scripts/ecosystem-charts/10-lineage.mjs` on pull request #6. Four rows are the Satoshi lineage: Bitcoin Core; Bitcoin Roots, a patch series on Bitcoin Core v32.1 that also carries selected Knots policy features; Knots Legacy, which continues Bitcoin Knots v29.3.knots20260507; and Bit-Block, a fork of Bitcoin Knots v29.1.knots20250903. Bitcoin Knots itself is not a row on the page. The other eight rows have no derivation from Core or Knots stated in the data and are grouped by primary language from `data/stack.json` `languages`.
entries.caveats: "Separate" means no derivation is stated in this page's data. rbitcoin carries Bitcoin Core as a git submodule (`stack.json` `vendored`); that is not counted as a derivation.

entries.name: Reachable-node share
entries.what: Share of reachable nodes by advertised user agent.
entries.why: It shows how much of the live network runs one lineage.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Formal spec
entries.what: A written, formal consensus specification separate from the code.
entries.why: Without a spec to check against, an alternative has to copy Core's behavior from Core, which keeps it tied to Core.
entries.how: Qualitative reading of each project's public repository, with a source link on yes or partial cells.
entries.caveats: On this reading, only BLVM is yes (the Orange Paper, with a Lean model of part of it). Hornet is partial. The rest are not found. A not-found cell is not a claim that no spec exists.

entries.name: Test vectors
entries.what: Conformance against shared test vectors, such as Bitcoin Core's JSON vectors.
entries.why: Shared vectors are a common check that two implementations accept and reject the same cases.
entries.how: Public-repository reading, with a source link. This is a yes/partial/not-found status, not the file count in the metrics table.
entries.caveats: "Yes" does not mean every vector file is run, or run to completion. BLVM runs every committed script and transaction row, and skips a row only for a named reason. libbitcoin and rbitcoin are partial. Hornet is not found.

entries.name: Property tests
entries.what: Property-based tests (proptest, quickcheck, and similar).
entries.why: They check general rules over many generated cases, not only fixed examples.
entries.how: Public-repository reading, with a source link. Distinct from the `test_property` line-count in `metrics.json`.
entries.caveats: satd and btcd are partial. Most Core-family rows are not found.

entries.name: Fuzzing
entries.what: Fuzz targets in the tree.
entries.why: Fuzzing feeds unexpected inputs to consensus and protocol code.
entries.how: Public-repository reading, with a source link. The yes/partial status is separate from the numeric `metrics.json` `fuzz_targets` count (see Code health).
entries.caveats: btcd is partial. libbitcoin and Hornet are not found. Core-family yes cells include fuzz harnesses carried from Core.

entries.name: Formal verification
entries.what: Machine-checked proofs or model checking of code.
entries.why: A proof can show that a function or a sentence of a spec holds, beyond passing tests.
entries.how: Public-repository reading, with a source link.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Differential vs Core
entries.what: Tests that compare verdicts with Bitcoin Core or its libraries.
entries.why: An independent implementation only helps if it can show it enforces the same rules as everyone else.
entries.how: Public-repository reading, with a source link.
entries.caveats: Bitcoin Core is n/a. BLVM's cell states script verdicts against libbitcoinconsensus and block accept or reject against libbitcoinkernel in blvm-bench, and says "No full-chain result is claimed here." Do not describe any row as having a full-chain differential result.

entries.name: Governance model
entries.what: A short label for who can change the tree and how.
entries.why: The people who can land a change are the people who can change the rules the network runs.
entries.how: `governance_model.labels[].label`, as of 2026-11-12. The file's note: labels are read from the institution board and the commit and merge shares on this page, and are redone with each reading. Current labels: Commons governance (BLVM); maintainer group with merge rights (Bitcoin Core); foundation, one signing key (Bitcoin Roots); single maintainer (Knots Legacy, Bit-Block, bitcoin-rs, satd, libbitcoin, Hornet); not classified (Floresta, rbitcoin, btcd).
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Written rules published by Bitcoin Commons
entries.what: Written rules for how node software changes, published by Bitcoin Commons: signatures by repository layer, review periods, and a governance-node quorum.
entries.why: They make the change process visible.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats: BLVM is the only implementation here that uses these rules. This page does not score a future projection.

entries.name: Landing share
entries.what: Share of each project's landing measure held by the account its history names.
entries.why: It is the operating record of who actually lands work, which can differ from the written rule.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Stated consequence vs norm
entries.what: A reading of whether a project's files state a consequence for breaking a process rule.
entries.why: A rule with a stated consequence is different from a stated practice with no sanction.
entries.how: `scan.rule_test`: a statement that names a consequence is a rule, and a statement that names none is a norm. Applied to the files and history this scan actually has. Judgment scores are not printed, because they are not measurements.
entries.caveats: Several trees have a contributing or code-owners file that this scan did not read as a stated consequence. satd, Floresta, rbitcoin, and btcd were not read for a rule file.

entries.name: Jurisdiction
entries.what: "This scan does not record where a maintainer sits. There is no jurisdiction chart."

entries.name: Implementation code
entries.what: Size of the program the rules sit in, in code lines.
entries.why: It is the volume of first-party code a reader has to take on trust, before tooling is removed.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats: Compare only with the same counter. BLVM's crate set is listed in the size caption. libbitcoin is one repo: libbitcoin-system. Nine trees only.

entries.name: Program code
entries.what: Implementation code minus tooling.
entries.why: It is the program itself, with tooling taken out.
entries.how: Same counter. Tooling is files the role map marks as tooling.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Checkout
entries.what: Program, test lines, tooling, vendored code, and locale files, in code lines.
entries.why: It is the size of the tree a checkout actually holds, including code that is not the program.
entries.how: Sum of `program_code`, the test-line split, `tooling_code`, `vendored_code`, and `locale_code` on the same counter.

entries.name: Tooling
entries.what: Files the role map marks as tooling.
entries.why: Tooling is part of the tree but is not the program the rules sit in.
entries.how: Same counter, role-map bucket.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Rules share
entries.what: Share of implementation on the rules side of that tree's cut, as a percent of implementation.
entries.why: It is one reading of how much of the tree is consensus-rule code, not a grade.
entries.how: Same-profile only: the Core file cut, the crate-role cut, and the repository-role cut are separate instruments and are not compared across profiles. Key: `tree_methods` id `rules_share`; `trees[].instrument` names the cut.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Left mixed
entries.what: Share of implementation left in a crate or library the cut did not split.
entries.why: A high mixed share means a large part of the tree was not placed on either side of the rules cut.
entries.how: Same instrument as rules share.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Tests per implementation line
entries.what: Test-bucket code lines divided by implementation code lines.
entries.why: It is a density ratio, not a claim about test quality.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats: The shorter page note at `scan.test_placement` / the size-table test caption still mentions only `*_test.rs` and `#[cfg(test)]`, and is narrower than the method actually used.

entries.name: Vendored code
entries.what: Bundled libraries, in code lines. Outside first-party code.
entries.why: Vendored source is code the node runs that is not first-party, counted separately from direct dependencies.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Locale
entries.what: Translation files, in code lines. Outside first-party code.
entries.why: Locale files can be large and are not program code.
entries.how: Same counter, locale-path bucket (`is_locale`).
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Lines in files of 1,000 or more
entries.what: How much of the program sits in large files, as a percent of program code.
entries.why: It is one reading of how concentrated the program is in large files.
entries.how: `share_ge_1000` in the measure script. Tooling is outside this share. Spec lock is tooling on BLVM.

entries.name: Files holding half the program
entries.what: Smallest set of program files whose code lines reach half the program code.
entries.why: It is one reading of how widely or narrowly the program is spread across files.
entries.how: `files_holding_half` in the measure script. Tooling is outside this count.

groups.name: Code health — tests, authors, CI, plugins

entries.name: Fuzz targets
entries.what: Number of declared fuzz targets at the pinned commit, not a count of files in a fuzz directory.
entries.why: It is a count of harnesses in the tree, not hours of fuzzing or bugs found.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: In-source test lines
entries.what: Test-bucket code lines that sit next to program sources, including in-file `#[cfg(test)]` and C++ `src/test`.
entries.why: It shows how much test code lives beside the program, as a folder split.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats: This is a folder split, not a unit-versus-integration classification. `test_unit` is a deprecated alias of this field and should not be labeled "unit tests."

entries.name: Test-folder test lines
entries.what: Remaining test-bucket files under `tests/`, `test/`, `e2e/`, `qa/`, or `functional/`.
entries.why: It shows tests kept in a dedicated test directory.
entries.how: Same `test_split` method.
entries.caveats: `test_integration` is a deprecated alias of this field and should not be labeled "integration tests."

entries.name: Fuzz test lines
entries.what: Test-bucket code lines under fuzz paths (`fuzz/`, `fuzz_targets/`, `src/test/fuzz/`).
entries.why: It is the size of fuzz-related test code, not the number of targets.
entries.how: Same `test_split` partition.
entries.caveats: Do not confuse this line count with `fuzz_targets`.

entries.name: Property test lines
entries.what: Test-bucket code lines whose path or name contains `property`, `proptest`, `quickcheck`, `hypothesis`, or `orange_paper_property`.
entries.why: It is a line-count companion to the verification-table property-tests status.
entries.how: Same `test_split` partition.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Test-split total
entries.what: Sum of the test-split buckets.
entries.why: It is the total test-bucket lines under the same counter.
entries.how: Sum of the `test_split` parts.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Test-vector files
entries.what: Count of files whose path or name looks like a test vector.
entries.why: It is a file count, not a claim that every file is executed.
entries.how: `count_vector_and_spec_files`. Path or name looks like a test vector (`vector`, `tx_valid`, `tx_invalid`, `script_tests`, `sighash`, `bipN`) with suffix `.json`, `.csv`, or `.hex`.
entries.caveats: Distinct from the verification-table `test_vectors` status. Name matching can miss or over-count files.

entries.name: Spec files
entries.what: Count of documentation or model files whose name looks like a spec.
entries.why: It is a file count, not a formal-spec status.
entries.how: `count_vector_and_spec_files`. Name looks like a spec (`spec`, `THE_ORANGE_PAPER`, orange paper, `bipN`) with suffix `.md`, `.rst`, `.txt`, `.lean`, or `.tex`. LICENSE and contributing files are excluded.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Human authors, 12 months
entries.what: Distinct human commit authors on the landing-share repo set in the last 12 months.
entries.why: It is a head-count of people who landed commits in the window, after aliases are merged and bots are dropped — not a measure of review or of governance.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Tagged releases, 12 months
entries.what: Git tags whose creator date falls in the 12-month window.
entries.why: It is a release-cadence count, not a stability grade.
entries.how: `releases_12m`. Annotated tags use the tagger date; lightweight tags use the tagged commit date (`creatordate`). Names that contain `/` (Go module subpath tags) are excluded. BLVM's note: blvm-node tags.
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: CI workflows
entries.what: Number of GitHub Actions workflow files at the pin.
entries.why: It is a file count, not a measure of coverage or of whether jobs pass.
entries.how: Number of `.github/workflows/*.{yml,yaml}` files at the pin (`parse_ci`).
entries.caveats_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: CI jobs
entries.what: GitHub Actions jobs at the pin, after expanding static matrices.
entries.why: It is a job-definition count, not a pass/fail record.
entries.how: `parse_ci` and `expand_matrix`. A static matrix of lists is expanded (an include-only matrix is just the include rows, not one implicit job plus those rows; minus exclude). A `fromJSON(needs.job.outputs.x)` matrix is expanded when the default non-PR value is written in the same workflow, or when the producer reads this tree's fuzz/Cargo.toml `[[bin]]` list. Unquoted `run:` scalars that break PyYAML are quoted and retried. If a matrix still cannot be expanded or a file still fails to parse, the cell is partial and the value is a lower bound.
entries.caveats: On pull request #9's head every `ci_jobs` cell is marked measured, not partial. The method still says a partial lower bound is what should be stored when expansion or parsing fails.

entries.name: Plugin or module system
entries.what: Whether the pinned tree's docs describe a module or plugin system; how many own-team optional modules; how many independently maintained modules.
entries.why: It describes how the node can be extended, not whether extensions are safe.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats: Most rows are no, with independently maintained modules not found. "No" is a reading of the tree's docs at the pin.

entries.name: License
entries.what: The repository's license file.
entries.why: It states the terms under which the code can be used and forked.
entries.how: The license file at the pin, with a source link. The method text states that no proprietary or non-OSI license file turned up in any tree.

entries.name: Languages
entries.what: Languages with 5% or more of code lines.
entries.why: It is the language mix of the tree, and the grouping key for separate codebases on the lineage chart.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data

entries.name: Direct third-party dependencies
entries.what: Direct third-party libraries of a default node build. BLVM is the minimal release instead of the default feature set.
entries.why: Each direct dependency is code the node pulls in from outside the project.
entries.how_omitted: contains figures; the page shows them from data
entries.caveats: Counts are not transitive. BLVM's cell is the minimal feature, counted 2026-11-12 from the local trees named in that row. The node pin on the row is the rest of the cut, not this dependency resolve.

entries.name: Vendored (stack table)
entries.what: Library subtrees or `vendor/` directories in the tree, with code lines rounded.
entries.why: Same as vendored code, above.
entries.how: Qualitative plus rounded line counts in the stack method.
entries.caveats: Prefer `trees[].values.vendored_code` when it is measured. See the disagreements listed under Vendored code. Floresta, rbitcoin, and btcd have only this stack field: Floresta and btcd "None found"; rbitcoin "None in the tree. Bitcoin Core is a git submodule."
